rationale: The five-year cumulative reformulation is a defensible, non-cosmetic response to the Buy-vs-Build diagnostic (persistent state variable rather than transaction-year flow), but it is largely the multiplicative superposition of two already-published effects — the acquisition/asset-growth anomaly and the R&D-intensity anomaly — so the incremental content is the interaction alone.

This is the archive's Buy-Versus-Build expression left "untouched" (the reasoning admits it) with only WINSOR and IND_ZSCORE wrappers appended — precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against — and winsorizing does not fix the ratio's real pathology, a denominator (capx+aqc+xrd) that can approach zero or flip sign.

Extending the gross-margin moat gate to the working-capital channel is a substantively different investment margin rather than a restatement, but the base leg is close to the published inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas–Zhang, Belo–Lin) and the two legs share cogs/sale mechanically, so a chunk of the spread may be an inventory-turnover/industry bet rather than a moat conditioning effect.

This is the first long-side, positively signed construct in the pair's archive and the interaction is genuinely required for the story (neither leg alone identifies knowledge-driven scaling), though the reviewer should expect the sales-growth leg to fight the signal since high sales growth is itself a documented negative predictor, and the R&D-stock leg reintroduces a known level anomaly.

A second-moment investment channel is a real addition to an archive that has only tested levels, changes and accelerations and has a plausible route around CMA, but VOL over five annual observations is a very noisy estimator that will load on small, lumpy, asset-light firms, so any spread needs a size and coverage-stability diagnostic before it is believed.

Stripped of its wrappers this is simply capex-vs-R&D investment intensity — a well-worn intangible-intensity measure that is close to a monotone transform of the published R&D-intensity anomaly rather than a cross-theme interaction — and it carries a construction defect the industry z-score cannot repair: a one-year capex flow is divided by a sum containing three years of R&D, mechanically pushing every research-active firm toward the low end for horizon reasons rather than economic ones.
